description: QORVEXIA is a team of students from Egypt passionate about Artificial Intelligence, programming, electronics, engineering, and space exploration. We combine software development, technical research, and engineering skills to solve real-world challenges. Our goal is to create innovative solutions that support astronaut health monitoring during space missions. We welcome collaboration, creativity, and learning as one team.

details:
. End-to-End System Architecture & Data Journey

The QORVEXIA pipeline operates across three deterministic stages designed to maximize signal accuracy, eliminate physical burden on astronauts, and protect sensitive biomedical data from capture to ground control.

Stage 1: Zero-Friction Biometric Acquisition (Fitbit Air Band)

Conventional clinical telemetry systems—such as wired Holter monitors, adhesive chest patches, and bulky finger pulse oximeters—cause skin irritation, mechanical friction, and restricted mobility inside spacesuits and compact habitats. QORVEXIA replaces these with the Google Fitbit Air Band, an ultra-lightweight, screenless biometric wearable.

  • Screenless Ergonomics: Built without an external glass display, the woven textile strap eliminates shatter hazards, unnecessary battery drain, and visual distraction during high-focus orbital tasks.
  • Multi-Sensor Physiological Array: Combining a 250 Hz optical photoplethysmography (PPG) array with a continuous single-lead dry-contact electrocardiogram (ECG) sensor, the wearable captures high-resolution cardiac waveforms alongside skin temperature, respiratory rate, and galvanic skin response (GSR).
  • Low-Power Wireless Link: Biometric frames stream continuously to the cabin receiver via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) 5.4, maintaining a -64 dBm signal link with over 94% battery efficiency.
  • Baseline Clinical Vitals: In nominal operation, the system tracks Heart Rate (71–72 BPM), Blood Oxygen Saturation (98.3%–98.5% SpO2), and Beat-to-Beat Heart Rate Variability (HRV rMSSD at 54.8–58.0 ms), identifying early autonomic stress long before physical symptoms appear.
